meta.title: Random Forest
meta.subtitle: Implementation of Random Forest for Classification

sections.text: To implement and understand the Random Forest algorithm for classification tasks, apply it to a real-world multiclass dataset, and evaluate its predictive performance using standard classification metrics. The experiment further aims to develop practical insight into how ensemble methods improve upon individual decision trees.

items: Understand the Random Forest classification mechanism and its underlying working principle.
Implement the Random Forest algorithm on a dataset for multiclass classification.
Evaluate the model using relevant metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

sections.text: Use a vitamin deficiency disease dataset to demonstrate the application of the Random Forest algorithm for multiclass classification. The task is to classify individuals into disease categories - Anemia, Healthy, Night_Blindness, Rickets_Osteomalacia, and Scurvy - based on demographic, lifestyle, and nutritional features.

Random Forest is a supervised ensemble learning algorithm that builds a large collection of decision trees during training and outputs the class that is the mode of the individual trees' predictions. Each tree is trained on a random subset of the data and considers a random subset of features at each split.
At each node split, only m features (m < p) are randomly selected, and the best split is chosen using an impurity criterion such as Gini impurity:
For classification, the final predicted class label for an input x is obtained by aggregating the predictions of all B trees h<sub>b</sub>(x):

rows: Number of decision trees built in the forest. More trees generally improve stability and accuracy but increase computation time.
Maximum depth allowed for each decision tree. Controls overfitting; shallow trees underfit, very deep trees overfit.

items: Import NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib and the required Scikit-learn modules.
Load the dataset and inspect its head, shape, information, and missing-value counts.
Split the data into training and testing sets using an 80:20 ratio with random_state=42.
Train the Random Forest model and evaluate it on the test set.

sections.text: In this experiment, a Random Forest classifier was successfully implemented on the vitamin deficiency disease dataset to perform multiclass classification. The ensemble-based approach achieved a high overall test accuracy of 95%, highlighting both the strength of Random Forest as a robust ensemble method and the importance of addressing class imbalance for underrepresented categories.
